newsitem.title: USA: TENNIS-WOODBRIDGE/WOODFORDE WIN AT WORLD DOUBLES CHAMPIONSHIP. [CORRECTED 4:20 GMT]
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-WOODBRIDGE/WOODFORDE WIN AT WORLD DOUBLES CHAMPIONSHIP. [CORRECTED 4:20 GMT]

text.p: The top-ranked team of Todd Woodbridge and Mark Woodforde needed only 63 minutes to dispose of Libor Pimek of Belgium and Byron Talbot of South Africa in their opening match of the Phoenix/ATP Tour World Doubles Championship on Wednesday.
The Australians, winners of 40 career titles in their five years together, showed efficiency throughout in a 6-2 6-3 victory.
"We couldn't ask for a better start. Hopefully we're on our way to a good week," said Woodforde, who served out the final game in a match which lacked suspense.
"This would top our year off, even though we'll remain number one whether we win or not. We've both had good singles years and that definitely has helped our doubles."
All eight teams continue in the round robin competition Thursday and Friday, with the top four advancing to Saturday's semifinals.
In another opening-day match, the fourth-ranked team of Jacco Eltingh and Paul Haarhuis of the Netherlands outgunned American Alex O'Brien and Sebastien Lareau of Canada 7-6 (7-2) 6-4.
Eltingh and Haarhuis were torrid from the net, especially in the second set. The only service break was off O'Brien in the final game.
Because of injuries to Eltingh, the Dutch team saw its ranking drop to 29th before a late run which included a finals berth in the U.S. Open and titles in Toulouse and Paris.
"Everybody knows we've been the best team this fall and it's nice to come into this tournament with a winning attitute," said Haarhuis. "We both have our confidence back."
Also getting an opening-day victory were Jonas Bjorkman and Nicklas Kulti of Sweden, who outlasted Mark Knowles of the Bahamas and Daniel Nestor of Canada 4-6 6-4 6-4.
The win was especially sweet for the Swedes because they had lost to Knowles and Nestor earlier this year.

In the final match of the night, second-ranked Byron Black of Zimbabwe and Grant Connell of Canada recovered from an error-filled first set to turn back American Trevor Kronemann and Australian David Macpherson 3-6 6-2 6-3.
Black and Connell, winners of four tournaments and finalists at Wimbledon this year, took the first three games of the final set and had little trouble running it out.
